audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags it directly: Kled wins 53.03% over 462 games but the chart handed Sett 4 of 7 stages to Kled's 1. Level 1 was given to Sett while phases[0].why says mounted stats bully every level-1 exchange.
audit.why: At level 1 Sett has only Knuckle Down (two empowered attacks, no gap-closer, no Grit stored) while Kled has mounted stats and an 800-range Bear Trap. Level 2 is genuinely even: Violent Tendencies beats an unstored Haymaker, but the damage you deal feeds his Grit.
audit.corrected: Row 0 -> Kled (7/10), row 1 -> Skill (5/10), proposed as paired full+content rows. Rows 2 and 4 stay Sett: Facebreaker at 3 and The Show Stopper at 6 are real swings.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text called The Show Stopper a 'suppress-slam' that 'wall-pins' and gave no numbers.
audit.why: Riot's text says he carries a champion through the air and slams them, slowing enemies near the landing point — no suppression or wall-pin is stated. It is 400 range on a 120s cooldown at rank 1, so it needs him already on top of you, which is what Facebreaker is for.
audit.corrected: spikes[2] and mid rewritten with the range/cooldown and the Facebreaker setup.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two decisive interactions in this lane were never stated, and percent-health damage was attributed to the wrong champion.
audit.why: (a) Facebreaker pulls in enemies on OPPOSITE sides of Sett and stuns them; if you are on one side only, you are merely slowed. That single rule decides where you stand for every trade. (b) Haymaker deals true damage in the centre of the punch and physical on the sides, so the edge of the cone is survivable. (c) Percent-max-health damage is Sett's Knuckle Down, not Kled's Bear Trap — Kled Q is flat physical plus a yank and has no percentHealth flag.
audit.corrected: Facebreaker's both-sides rule and Haymaker's centre-only true damage now appear in early, mid, report[5], breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0] and dontsFull[1]; every 'Q percent-HP shred' replaced with the Bear Trap yank.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1] was titled 'Get E-stunned' but its body text was about wasting Q on the wave.
audit.why: Copy-paste from a generic template; the body did not describe the mistake in the title.
audit.corrected: Body replaced with the far-side rule that actually explains the stun.

edits.before: Sett wants to face-tank and out-grit you, but your level 2 flips that — once W (Violent Tendencies) is up, your Jousting Proc shots fire faster than he can store his W (Haymaker), so a short trade goes your way. Open with Q (Bear Trap) for the slow and percent-HP chunk, then E through him, dump W shots, and E back out before his grab lands. The thing to dodge is his E (Facebreaker) grab-stun — if he pulls you, eat a free smash plus his passive double-punch, so never trade standing still in his face.
edits.after: Sett wants to face-tank and out-grit you, but your level 2 flips that — once Violent Tendencies is up, four fast attacks land before he has stored the Grit that pays for Haymaker, so a short trade goes your way. Open with Bear Trap for the slow and yank, then E through him, dump the W attacks, and E back out before his grab lands. Facebreaker only stuns if enemies are on BOTH sides of him — keep the wave off your far side and his 490-range grab is a slow, not a stun.

edits.before: This is where Sett claws it back. By levels 4-6 his stored W true damage and bruiser grit start eating Skaarl's health bar in any drawn-out trade, and at 6 his R (suppress-slam) can wall-pin you for a guaranteed W combo — that's his biggest single threat in the lane. Keep your trades SHORT here: Q-slow, quick E-W burst, leave. Don't get greedy on a remount when his W is stored and his grab is up, or he flips a coinflip trade into a kill.
edits.after: This is where Sett claws it back. By levels 4-6 stored Grit turns Haymaker's true-damage centre into a chunk of Skaarl's bar in any drawn-out trade, and at 6 The Show Stopper carries you off for a guaranteed follow-up — his biggest single threat in the lane. Keep your trades SHORT here: Bear Trap, quick E-W burst, leave. Don't get greedy on a remount when his W is stored and Facebreaker is up, or he flips a coinflip trade into a kill.

edits.before: Past first item it levels out — you still bully him in a clean short-trade all-in with Q percent-HP shred and remount sustain, but his stored-W true damage ignores your bulk and his R is a teamfight engage you can't fully answer 1v1. Use R (Chaaaaaaaaarge!!!) to roam and snowball the lead your early window gave you rather than forcing one more risky lane all-in. Win the game off tempo, not off out-statting a Sett who's now built to take hits.
edits.after: Past first item it levels out — you still bully him in a clean short-trade all-in with the Bear Trap yank and remount sustain, but Haymaker's true damage ignores your bulk and his R is a teamfight engage you can't fully answer 1v1. notes: Sett's R carries the 'grounding' derived flag but Riot's description says nothing about grounding or suppression, so I described only what the text supports (carry, slam, slow on landing) and did not assert dash denial — worth checking on the wiki before anyone writes that Kled's E is disabled by it. Kled's W is Violent Tendencies; 'Jousting Proc shots' (Jousting is his E) appeared twice here and is a repeat of the same champion-wide naming error.
